page.title: Runners and queue
page.lead: Machines that run builds and checks, and the jobs waiting for them.

secret.hint: Copy it now and pass it to whoever starts the runner.
secret.commandHint: Run it on the runner machine. The Studio address and the secret are already filled in; after the first start the runner stores its own token and the value can be removed from the environment.

noneOnline.title: No runner is online
noneOnline.body: Builds and checks wait in the queue until a runner connects. Check that the runner machines are up and can reach the server.

empty.title: No runners yet
empty.body: Without runners nothing gets built. Create a registration token and start a runner with it on any machine.

rotateDialog.title: New token for {{name}}
rotateDialog.body: The previous runner token stops working and the runner loses its connection until it receives the new one. The secret is shown once.

rotated.title: New token for {{name}}
rotated.lead: The previous token no longer works.
rotated.label: Runner token

revoke.title: Revoke runner
revoke.body: The runner loses access and stops taking jobs. Jobs it is running are handed to another runner.

tokens.title: Registration tokens
tokens.lead: A one-time secret a new runner uses to obtain its own token.
tokens.howTo: To connect a runner: create a token, run the command shown on the runner machine, and it appears in the table above within seconds.

empty.title: No tokens
empty.body: Create a token when you need to connect a new runner.

form.title: New registration token
form.lead: The secret is shown once, right after it is created.
form.label: Name
form.labelHint: So you can tell later what it was for: for example, the server in room 305.
form.maxUsesHint: From 1 to 100. The token stops working after the last connection.
form.maxUsesInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 100.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke token
revokeDialog.body: Token "{{label}}" will stop accepting new runners. Runners already connected keep working.

empty.title: The queue is empty
empty.body: Jobs appear here when someone starts a build or a check.

errors.job_timeout: The job time limit was exceeded
errors.timed_out: The job time limit was exceeded
errors.artifact_invalid: The runner returned a damaged result
errors.blob_missing: A project file was not found
errors.storage_unreachable: The runner cannot reach the storage: the administrator must set a public S3 address
errors.artifact_upload_failed: The runner could not upload its result to the server
errors.unknown: The job finished with an error

cancelDialog.title: Cancel job
cancelDialog.body: The "{{kind}}" job of {{user}} will be stopped.
cancelDialog.running: It is already running: the runner will interrupt it and the result will not be saved.

personal.title: Personal runners
personal.lead: People's machines that build their own projects. Jobs on them don't use installation quotas; only the runner's owner can rotate its token.
personal.onlineHint: Personal runners taking jobs right now.
personal.search: Search by owner or runner name
personal.caption: Personal runners

empty.title: No personal runners
empty.body: People connect them in their account settings: the Studio on a computer or a console runner.

personal.noMatch: Nothing found. Change the search or filter.

disabled.title: Personal runners are off
disabled.body: People's builds use shared runners and quotas, AI via runners doesn't work.

personal.revokeBody: Runner "{{name}}" of {{owner}} stops getting jobs right away. This can't be undone: the owner will have to connect the machine again.
personal.pausedHint: Paused: the runner polls but takes no jobs.
personal.ownersHint: People who have a runner of their own

gateway.title: AI gateway
gateway.lead: The installation's shared AI providers over the last day. The circuit breaker closes a provider after a run of failures and tries it again later.
gateway.loadFailed: Could not load the gateway state.
gateway.emptyHint: Add a shared AI provider under Installation.

autoscale.title: Autoscaling
autoscale.lead: The number of shared runners follows the queue. The server does not start runners itself: it asks an orchestrator (docker compose or an external webhook) to reach the number.
autoscale.invalid: Check the values: the ceiling is not below the minimum and the address starts with http.

reason.queue_depth: the queue is longer than normal
reason.queue_wait: a task waits longer than the threshold
reason.cooldown_up: cooling down after growth, {{seconds}} s left
reason.idle: the queue is empty and runners are free
reason.idle_wait: the queue is empty, waiting out the idle window, {{seconds}} s left
reason.cooldown_down: cooling down after a change, {{seconds}} s left
reason.at_min: at the minimum, the queue is empty
reason.balanced: the queue is within the norm

hint.off: The decision is computed and shown here; nothing is started.
hint.compose: The server runs `docker compose up --scale`. It needs docker and daemon access where the api runs; project and file come from the environment.
hint.webhook: The server sends a POST with the wanted runner count. Plug in Nomad, a Kubernetes operator or your own script.

url.label: Webhook address
url.hintSigned: The body is signed with HMAC-SHA256 (header X-Autoscale-Signature); the secret is set in the environment.
url.hintUnsigned: No signing secret is set in the environment: the request goes unsigned.

min_runners.label: Minimum runners
min_runners.hint: Never go below this number; below it we grow at once.

target_queue_per_slot.label: Waiting tasks per slot
target_queue_per_slot.hint: Grow when the queue per slot is above this number.

scale_up_wait_s.label: Wait threshold
scale_up_wait_s.hint: Grow when the oldest task waits longer.

cooldown_down_s.label: Cooldown before shrinking
cooldown_down_s.hint: Pause after any change before shrinking.

idle_before_down_s.label: Idle window
idle_before_down_s.hint: How long the queue must stay empty before shrinking.

step_up.label: Growth step
step_up.hint: How many runners to add at once.

step_down.label: Shrink step
step_down.hint: How many runners to remove at once.

install.title: Install a runner
install.lead: A runner executes builds and checks. Pick where to put it.
install.name: Runner name
install.nameHint: Optional. A short suffix is added so you can install several runners.
install.capabilitiesFailed: Could not find out what can be installed on this machine.
install.busy: An install of this kind is already running. Wait for it to finish.

docker.title: Docker next to the Studio
docker.lead: The Studio starts a runner container through its docker.sock. The runner survives restarts and connects by itself.

kubernetes.title: Deployment in the cluster
kubernetes.lead: The Studio creates a runner Deployment in its namespace under a separate ServiceAccount allowed to touch build pods only.

docker.no_socket: The Studio cannot see docker.sock. In the default install it has no Docker access on purpose: the socket is root on the host. Use the SSH install or the command next to the token.
docker.docker_unreachable: docker.sock exists, but Docker does not answer or the Studio has no right to the socket.
docker.no_permission: The Studio has no rights to Docker.

kubernetes.disabled: Turned off in the chart (runner.installFromUi.enabled). Shared runners are off on production on purpose, so there is no button by default.
kubernetes.not_in_cluster: The Studio does not run inside a Kubernetes cluster.
kubernetes.no_permission: The Studio ServiceAccount may not create a Deployment, Secret and volume in its namespace.

command.title: On another machine
command.lead: Get a token and a ready docker run command or a service script and run it there.

install.succeeded: The runner is installed and connected to the Studio.

error.unexpected: The install failed for an unexpected reason. See the Studio log for details.
error.image_pull_failed: Could not pull the runner image. Check that Docker can reach the registry.
error.container_start_failed: Docker could not start the container.
error.kube_forbidden: The cluster refused the request. Check the Studio ServiceAccount Role.
error.kube_failed: The cluster returned an error while creating resources.
error.register_timeout: The runner started but did not connect to the Studio within three minutes. Check that it can reach the Studio address and retry.
